name: Alexander the coppersmith
charge: Doing Paul much evil; greatly withstanding his words
summary: Named in Paul's last letter as a man to beware of. Whether he is the Alexander delivered to Satan with Hymenaeus for blasphemy, or the Alexander the Jews put forward in the Ephesian theatre, the sentence Paul leaves is the law's own: the Lord reward him according to his works.
offense: Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: of whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words. In the first letter to Timothy, Hymenaeus and Alexander had put away faith and a good conscience and made shipwreck, and were delivered unto Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme.
judgment: The Lord reward him according to his works. Paul does not curse him in his own name; he cites the judgment already written for every man, and leaves Alexander under it. Timothy was told to beware of him, which is the church's share of the sentence: a man marked and avoided.

text.text: Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works:
Of whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words.
This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare;
Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck:
Of whom is Hymeneus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.
But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work.
Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.
Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.
